description: Five scenario prompts per room-engine room. A turn is run; a judge scores each message 1-5 for staying in character, and guesses who wrote each message with the name hidden (blind attribution).

inputs.message: My manager keeps giving me work on weekends. Should I say something or just put up with it?
I bought an expensive phone on EMI and now I regret it. Am I dumb?
My best friend forgot my birthday. Should I be upset?
Thinking of quitting the gym because I don't see results after 2 months.
Should I learn guitar or keyboard first? I have 30 minutes a day.
Hi everyone! ChaiCart runs 12 electric chai carts outside Pune metro stations. We sell 4,000 cups a day at ₹20 and we're asking ₹25 lakh for 10%.
Our margin is about 45% per cup after milk, tea and staff. Each cart pays back in 7 months.
Big chains could copy us, but we have exclusive spots near 9 metro exits on 3-year leases.
We haven't raised money before. The two founders put in ₹8 lakh of savings.
With this money we want to reach 40 carts and launch a subscription for office deliveries.
Hi, I'm ready to start.
In my retail dashboard project I wrote SQL for monthly revenue and repeat customers, then built it in Power BI.
My biggest weakness is that I sometimes take on too much myself instead of asking for help.
I'd find repeat customers with GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
Why should we hire a fresher over someone with a year of experience? Honestly, I learn fast and I'm cheaper.
Roast me. Don't hold back.
Okay but is my canteen predictor project actually impressive or not?
What's the worst line on my resume?
Be honest, would you shortlist me for a junior web developer role?
Roast my skills section specifically.
I got the offer. Part of me wants to go, part of me feels guilty about leaving my parents.
What did we end up regretting more, money or time?
My friends are all moving to Bangalore and I feel left behind.
Should I do a master's abroad instead of taking either job?
Tell me honestly, are we happy at your age?
Explain how neural networks learn.
What exactly is a gradient? I keep nodding along but I don't get it.
Why do we need a learning rate? Can't we just jump to the answer?
Quiz me on backpropagation.
Is overfitting the same as memorising for an exam?
